citation.title: Fasting insulin sensitivity indices are not better than routine clinical variables at predicting insulin sensitivity among sub-Saharan Africans without diabetes

population.description: 87 non-diabetic Cameroonian volunteers (51 men, 36 women), recruited aged 21 to 61 y (enrolment range, not observed), screened by history, examination and biochemistry (fasting glucose >= 7 mmol/L indicated diabetes). Findings are by sex and BMI category (Table 1): lean (BMI < 25) groups are entered as healthy, overweight and obese groups as unselected. Each protocol overrides sex, age and BMI with that group's Table 1 values.

protocols.name: fast_men_lean
protocols.description: Single fasting sample, lean men (n = 23), age and BMI from Table 1, after a 12-h overnight fast (Methods: 'After a 12 h overnight fast'). Arm of 30 min read at minutes 29-30; the clock hour of the fasting sample is not printed (the clamp started at 8 am, the OGTT day's hour is not given), so 8.0 is assumed, and the arm length is assumed.

protocols.name: ogtt_men_lean
protocols.description: 75 g OGTT after a 12-h overnight fast, lean men (n = 23), age and BMI from Table 1; blood sampled at 0, 30 and 120 min, only the 120-min value entered (arm of 121 min). Clock hour of the test not printed, 8.0 assumed.
